Change Ringing Corpus · Method shapes

Every method,
as a shape

Ringers do not learn a method from its notation. They learn the line — the path one bell traces through it. This is that drawing, computed from the published place notation for 20,679 methods, laid out so whole families can be compared at a glance.

The wall

Each tile is one lead, drawn from rounds. Filter by stage and classification, or search a name. Click any tile for the full line and its rows.

Cambridge, Yorkshire, Superlative and Lincolnshire are the four standard Surprise Major methods most bands learn first. Filter to Surprise / Major and search each in turn: the family resemblance is immediate, and it is the reason ringers describe them as being “near” one another despite quite different notation.

Lines are computed from the place notation published by the CCCBR Methods Library, parsed by scripts/notation.py. Only methods whose parse is confirmed against the library’s own published lead_head are shown — the rest are excluded rather than drawn unchecked. Failures concentrate at odd stages; at Minor and Major, the stages drawn here, the parser agrees with the library on over 99.7% of methods.

Blue line diagrams are standard in ringing software. What is new here is drawing the whole collection at once, so families can be compared side by side.

Built from data/change-ringing.db by the scripts in scripts/; the SQL behind each page is in queries/, read at build time rather than copied, so the recorded queries are the ones that ran. Data derived from Dove’s Guide, the CCCBR Methods Library and BellBoard — CC BY-SA 4.0, see data/LICENCE-DATA.md before reusing it. The code is MIT.
